#3410. 8 Actors With the Most Iconic Voices in Film History

The right voice can resonate with audiences for generations to come. Speech is the best way to broadcast messages or persuade others to believe or adopt a certain way of thinking. We've needed the perfect voice for centuries. Leaders have built nations, commanded armies into battle, and braved a worried public through times of crisis, thanks to the power of their voices. Truly, it is the voice that commands our attention, and throughout cinema history, some actors had the right pitch.

Countless actors have come and gone on the big screen throughout the years since the invention of filmmaking, but few had the voices that instantly stuck with audiences. There are some with the voice that defined their careers, the ones with a certain way of speaking that was either powerful, memorable, or distinctly their own. These voices helped elevate the films these actors were in, and even influenced pop culture with the epic lines they delivered. From the raspy intensity of Al Pacino to the commanding resonance of James Earl Jones, here are the eight most iconic acting voices in film history.

Starting off is the one and only Al Pacino, the acclaimed Academy Award winner whose voice delivered some of the most recognizable lines in movie history. Widely considered one of the greatest actors of all time, Mr. Pacino made a name for himself playing some of cinema's biggest icons, from the menacing mob boss Michael Corleone in The Godfather to the charismatic union leader Jimmy Hoffa in The Irishman. Whether playing stern and reserved masterminds or loud, bombastic madmen, one thing is for sure: his voice sells the performance.

Best known today for his distinct raspy, gravelly voice, Al's way of speaking has become synonymous with his entire career, even though in his early years, he sounded much different. In the early days of The Godfather, Dog Day Afternoon, and Serpico, his voice was noticeably faster, hyper, and even higher-pitched, which helped him sound manic in scenes that required him to seem overwhelmed. But, after years of loud shouting on screen and an unhealthy smoking habit, his tone has slowly developed into its now recognizable gruffness that has become his signature trait. His voice has been referenced, parodied, and cherished by fans throughout the years, and it has helped cement his legacy as an unforgettable legend of the acting world.

There's no talking about iconic voices in movies without doing an impression of the legendary "Governator" himself, Arnold Schwarzenegger. A man who single-handedly defined the explosive epicenes of 1980s action movies, Arnie has become a staple of pop culture, a man who will be forever known thanks to his works in The Terminator, Predator, and Conan the Barbarian. Despite his intimating presence and Olympian physique, we instantly know it's him from that broad Austrian accent of his.

Born and raised in Thal, Styria, Austria, Schwarzenegger's pronounced voice and thick accent became his most beloved trait, one that has become immortalized in cinema. Going from his native German to speaking English in his acting career led to some unusual but awesome pronunciations that turned simple, ordinary movie lines, like "I'll be back!" and "Get to the choppa!", into some of the most quotable one-liners of all time. He created a legacy that so many fans and movie lovers adore and constantly reference. It really shaped him into the icon most of us know and love today.

A voice that forever shaped the tone of the famed 007 James Bond, the late great Sean Connery will always be synonymous with cinema's most revered gentleman spy. This Academy Award-winning icon of the 20th century defined what it meant to be a capable leading man on screen, an actor who never lost his touch throughout his decades-long career, who handled any performance, and was the best part of any film, no matter its quality. And it's mostly thanks to his noticeable, charming Lowland Scottish accent.

Let's admit it, any time we think of James Bond's signature line, "Shaken, not stirred," we mostly invision it being said with Connery's Scottish accent. The way he speaks is extremely his own, and he's made it present in everything he was in, even in roles where he wasn't supposed to be Scottish, like as the bold Russian Commander Marko Ramius in The Hunt for Red October or the immortal Egyptian Ramírez in Highlander. His voice exuded authority and charm the likes of which Hollywood, during his time, had never seen before. His charm and the way he pronounced words could have turned any simple speech or cheesy one-liner into an epic moment that demanded the audiences' attention. In other words, he was the man with a voice to prove it.

No voice can command so much power and authority in cinema these days as Liam Neeson's. This prolific and versatile leading man has had a helping hand in creating some of the riveting action thrillers, gripping dramas, and unexpectedly hilarious comedies from the last thirty years. A man who can lead the screen in any genre, he's achieved stardom through giving passionate performances, showing notable dedication to his craft, and, most especially, delivering his lines with a deep, gravelly voice that immediately draws you in.

Appearing in over 100 films since the late 1970s, Neeson has stood out spectacularly for his distinct voice that's certainly one-of-a-kind. Stern, sometimes calming, but always commanding, his deep voice, which has subtle hints of his Irish upbringing, immediately tells you to watch and hear what he has to say. Whether it's through playing heroic, mentorly roles like Aslan in The Chronicles of Narnia or calculating threats like Ra's al Ghul in Batman Begins, his voice exudes so much captivating power that so many actors can only dream of having. Honestly, no one has a voice quite like his.

Come pay respects to one of the greatest voices in all of pop culture. After his death in late 2026, the remarkable Peter Cullen left a void in the entertainment world that we'll never see again. A man whose voice spoke for generations but a face we rarely saw behind the characters he played; to say Mr. Cullen had a successful career in voice acting would be putting it lightly. And it's all thanks to his one-of-a-kind ability to change the tone and sound of his voice into something different with every role.

With over 200 documented voice credits under his belt, Peter Cullen's voice has simply been everywhere over the last half century, even when you didn't even realize it. From small parts in Gremlins, Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers, Knight Rider, and even the iconic clicking noises the Predator makes in Predator, his vocal talents were unique and different each time, but also so fascinating to hear. But, let's be real, we all know him best for one role only: the heroic Autobot leader Optimus Prime from the Transformers franchise. This was a role only he could truly bring to life, playing Prime with so much resonating depth and authority that it was simply hypnotic and unforgettable. Playing Prime was his legacy, and it will continue to be heard and enjoyed for generations to come.

If there's one voice that has defined the horror genre, it would be Vincent Price's distinct utterance. Having one of the most recognizable voices in all of cinema, Mr. Price cemented himself as a prolific and charming character actor, always able to give the most dedicated and noticeable performance, no matter how big or small the part is. A huge reason for this, of course, was his voice, which is so rich and hypnotic that it's the first thing you instantly remember about him.

Vincent Price's unique enunciations and the sophisticated tone of his voice were perfect for every role he played, especially in horror movies, which only enhanced the eerie mood or atmosphere. His voice expressed intelligence and grace whether he was soft-spoken or loud and domineering. You simply couldn't look away from the screen whenever he spoke. And of all the many iconic roles he played, we'll perhaps always remember him giving that chilling speech at the end of Michael Jackson's Thriller song.

We all knew this one was coming. Of course, no voice in movie history is more beloved than that of Morgan Freeman. A cherished icon of the acting world, who has given it his all in every role for nearly fifty years now, Morgan Freeman gripped us all in the story primarily due to his smooth, calming voice, which makes us just want to hear every single word he says.

From Glory, Shawshank Redemption, March of the Penguins to Million Dollar Baby and Bruce Almighty, Freeman's voice is largely the takeaway from all of these films, and he has plenty of more notable films under his belt. He delivers so much passion, resonating charm, and genuine interest in everything he says, which has lead to so many of his lines becoming the best in movie history.

Finally, at number one, we have the booming voice that has shaken cinema to its core, being heard all the way from the Pride Lands in The Lion King to a galaxy far, far away in Star Wars. We're, of course, talking about the late and legendary James Earl Jones, the voice of Darth Vader, Mufasa, and many, many more characters audiences will never forget.

James Earl Jones' incredibly deep and prominent voice has captivated audiences for decades. There is simply no other voice like his. It's one that can inspire hope or fill audiences with immense dread; it could soothe and calm people or instill fear or intimidate them. In other words, his voice can evoke all kinds of emotions, and the characters have become immortalized in pop culture because of it. He's sadly no longer with us, but his voice will echo throughout the years. Truly, he is the voice of entertainment.

Amazon is offering early Black Friday discounts on like-new versions of its 2024 Kindles, with prices starting at $152.99 for the Paperwhite and savings of $27 to $75 across five models that include the color-screen Colorsoft and the pen-equipped Kindle Scribe. All five are a generation behind Amazon's current lineup: The company introduced redesigned Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (plus accessories) in October, with the new Paperwhite now starting at $199.99, and replaced the 2024 Scribe with a third-generation model in December 2025. As for its “like-new” label, it means these are pre-owned devices that Amazon has tested and certified to look and work like new.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite (16GB) is down to $152.99 from $179.99 and covers just about everything most people need for everyday reading, including enough storage for thousands of ebooks. Its seven-inch, 300ppi glare-free display is larger than the previous generation’s 6.8-inch screen, with faster page turns, an adjustable warm light, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life. As PCMag notes in its review, it's a great option for readers who don't need color or handwriting features.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $190.99 from $224.99, making it just $38 more than the like-new Paperwhite (16GB). For that relatively small difference, you're doubling the storage to 32GB and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft (16GB) is down to $220.99 from $260.99 and offers something the Paperwhite models can’t: a color E-Ink display, which makes it well suited to comics, graphic novels, illustrated books, and travel guides. Its seven-inch screen shows that color content at 150ppi while keeping text at a sharp 300ppi, and you can mark passages in multiple highlight colors to keep your notes organized. That said, colors are noticeably more muted than on a conventional tablet, and battery life tops out at eight weeks, compared with 12 weeks on the Paperwhite.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $243.99 from $287.99, making it just $23 more than the standard like-new Colorsoft. For that modest increase, you're getting twice the storage at 32GB, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

The Like-New Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $284.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but prices aren’t always what they seem. Use a price tracker to make sure you’re getting the best deal, or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

#3408. Apple to open new Developer Center in Istanbul as part of broader Turkey investment

Apple today announced a long-term investment in Turkey, with seven new facilities focused on app development and manufacturing set to open in the country starting next year. Here are the details.

In a press release issued on its Turkish Newsroom (via MacRumors), Apple today announced a series of long-term investments in Turkey.

The announcement comes as former CEO and current executive chairman Tim Cook visits the country, as he’s been sharing on X.

Merhaba Istanbul! What a stunning view from the Grand Bazaar this morning alongside talented creator Cem Başak. Thrilled to visit this remarkable country! pic.twitter.com/c4daBBXe1l

The company’s investment in Turkey will be three-pronged, with the opening of five new Apple Developer Academies, one Apple Developer Center, and one Apple Manufacturing Academy.

Apple says it will open five new developer academies across Turkey over the next three years, with the first opening in Istanbul in 2027, alongside its new developer center. The Apple Manufacturing Academy, meanwhile, is set to open in Ankara in 2028.

Here’s Cook commenting on today’s announcement (translation ours):

“Apple has been serving our customers and communities in Turkey for 35 years. With this new commitment, we are proud to support the next generation of innovative entrepreneurs in the years ahead. […] Turkey’s developer community is developing apps used around the world. Meanwhile, small and medium-sized businesses stand out as organizations creating opportunities throughout the country. This investment provides developers and businesses with access to the training and resources they need to take their brightest ideas even further, as well as to Apple experts.”

Apple explained that its developer academies will offer “free, intensive nine-month programs focused on coding, design, marketing, project management, and artificial intelligence technologies,” while the developer center “will provide developers, entrepreneurs, and start-ups with a hands-on learning experience by providing access to the latest tools, technologies, and resources, as well as Apple experts and events.”

As for its manufacturing academy in Ankara, which will mark the company’s first Apple Manufacturing Academy outside the US, it will “provide free training and consultancy to small and medium-sized businesses, students and innovative entrepreneurs.”

Led by Apple experts, the curriculum will help participants adopt AI and intelligent manufacturing techniques through courses on machine learning technology, predictive maintenance, advanced automation, and robotics, as well as interactive workshops on lean operations and production efficiency.

In an increasingly volatile world shaped by extreme weather, power outages and cyberattacks, being prepared for an emergency is no longer seen as paranoia. Instead, governments are actively encouraging the public to stock up on emergency supplies to last for three days.

At the end of October, the U.K. government launched its "Be Ready” campaign, urging households to take to small steps to prepare for emergencies. It was unsettling to hear, but the public took it in its stride without pressing the panic button.

While I half expected grocery aisles to descend into chaos, the public’s response has been remarkably calm and considered. People are clearly listening, but without the fear.

According to research by Worldpanel by Numerator and reported by the BBC, following the campaign, sales of hand sanitizer, bottled water, and tinned and jarred items rose by 83%, 67%, and 37%, respectively, indicating that hygiene is top of the agenda.

The story is slightly different in the U.S., where the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) launched its Ready Campaign in 2003, empowering and educating Americans to “prepare for, respond to and mitigate emergencies and disasters.”

Although the U.S. is ahead in urging households to assemble an emergency kit, both share the same remit: encouraging people to have sufficient supplies for a few days.

In the U.K., households are being urged to keep three days’ worth of food and water on hand. That equates to three liters of drinking water per person, per day, excluding water for washing. As for food, the focus is on non-perishables that don’t require refrigeration or cooking if the power cuts out. Tinned meat and fish, vegetables, fruit and nuts are ideal, but do ensure you have a manual can opener.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The “Be Ready” campaign also recommends gathering essentials like torches, warm clothing, medical and hygiene products and cash in a mix of coins and notes.

But there’s another item to add to your emergency kit that will keep you connected if the networks go down. It might seem archaic, but a wind-up radio remains the most reliable lifeline for emergency broadcasts when the grid fails. And it’s the first item I added to my grab bag.

When the power goes out and the networks go down, a wind-up radio keeps you connected. That’s why it was the first item I bought on the back of the U.K. “Be Ready” campaign advice.

There are plenty of wind-up radios to choose from online, but I opted for an all-singing-all-dancing version that offers some extra benefits. My emergency Multi-Purpose Crank Radio, is $37.99 at Amazonand comes in a choice of four bright colorways — green, blue, orange and red. It’s bright enough to stand out if you need to find it in a hurry!

This emergency radio is designed for power outages and other emergencies. It can be manually charged by the hand crank or the solar panel, and it also has a compartment for AAA batteries. In addition to tuning into emergency radio broadcasts, it features a torch, a reading light and an emergency alarm.

On first inspection, you’ll notice it has a solar panel on top, but aside from relying on the sun to power it, it also has a wind-up crank that pulls out from the back and a battery compartment that fits 3 x AAA batteries. If you’re relying on manual power, you’ll need to turn the crank for 3-5 minutes to activate the internal battery for initial use — it's like a mini workout!

Dig a little more into the details, and you’ll find the crank needs to be turned at 130-150 rpm for power to be generated — taking 7 hours until it’s fully charged. I may be handing this one over to the Tom’s Guide fitness team

It also has two light options. Lift up the solar panel to reveal an LED reading light, or press the adjacent button to illuminate the flashlight. What’s more, if the light isn’t enough to help you find your way, or someone else find you, it has an SOS alarm on the base of the gadget — just cover your ears before you try it out!

On the same switch as the SOS alarm, you’ll also find the charging button, which you’ll need to select to recharge your phone. And when you do charge it up, there’s a USB port on the side by the antenna, and it includes a micro USB cable for connecting your devices. On the underside, you can also access the 2000 mAh rechargeable battery, by removing two small screws on the base.

I nearly forgot about the strap. It comes with a lanyard and carabiner, so you can attach it to your clothing and keep it on your person when needed. Depending on the size of your pockets, it could easily be pocket-sized. It measures 2.91 (h) x 6.18 (w) x 2.09 (d) inches.

Beneath all of these extra functions, it is still, first and foremost, a radio. While that makes it a prehistoric relic to my children, I’m a child of the 70s and grew up relying on a radio for the latest hits.

Switch to radio mode by selecting 'LI-ION' on the front. At the side of the radio, you’ll find the antenna; swivel it around and extend it for a better signal. Then select the required bandwidth; you can choose WB, FM or AM. The circular knobs control the volume (which also acts as the on/off button) and tuning.

As you get close to a station, a small green light appears on the tuning panel and stays on once a channel is properly selected.

If needed, the radio gives you access to NOAA weather broadcasts and keeps you informed with emergency alerts and local information.

My verdictI wouldn’t recommend running the radio, flashlight, reading light and SOS alarm simultaneously, but it’s one small gadget I’d recommend adding to your emergency pack. It’s intuitive to use, small to store, and a mini powerhouse.

#3405. Ring's New $250 Indoor Camera Drone Sounds Terrifying

Ring made its name with its smart doorbells with built-in cameras, and now sells more indoor cameras than any other company, capturing more than 40% of the market. When you've already moved tens of millions of devices (enough to raise serious concerns about their use as part of the surveillance state), you always need to keep innovating, and today, the company announced a product it has been working on for a decade: an indoor camera drone powered by artificial intelligence. I got a chance to check it out during a media event yesterday, and I can report that, as harbingers of our dystopian future go, it is only mildly terrifying.

The drone camera is one of two products in the company's new Ring Robotics line, alongside a "rover cam" that looks kind of like the canister of a vacuum cleaner attached to an iPad. While the Ring Rover Cam is priced at $999.99 and targeted at businesses, the Ring Drone Cam is a much more affordable $249.99, reasonable enough that it will appeal to consumers looking for another way to keep (robot) eyes on their stuff.

The drone camera records 2K video and has a 148-degree field of view and the ability to rotate 360 degrees. It works with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms, as well as the Alexa Home Map. It has a flight time of eight minutes, and once it returns to its base station, it takes around an hour to fully recharge (eight minutes on the dock will give it one minute in the air).

As Ring founder Jamie Siminoff explained during the preview event, the company has been trying to build a workable camera drone for around a decade, but couldn't overcome certain design challenges until the advancement of AI models that allow the device to handle most of the computing—from route programming to threat detection—via the cloud, so the drones can be smaller and lighter.

According to Ring, when setting up the Ring Drone Cam, you carry it around your house, allowing it to map the interior. It will "intelligently identify rooms and suggest patrol points: spots worth extra attention." When sent out on "patrol," the drone's AI pilot will travel between hotspots, sensing and avoiding furniture and other obstacles along the way.The Ring Drone Cam works with other Ring cameras, so if an alert is triggered somewhere in your home—say, a window opening unexpectedly—the drone will take off to investigate. It has a built-in security light that will make its presence known, so it can also act as a deterrent, though the screaming sound of its spinning propellers will accomplish that just as well.

According to Ring, the drone camera can deliver peace of mind whether you're home or away, and admittedly I do like the idea of being able to check on my pets or make sure no pipes have burst while I'm at work or on vacation (though admittedly you can get the same sort of monitoring without involving an AI device that looks like a mini version of the flying robots from The Terminator).

I admit that the Ring Drone Cam seems pretty cool, provided I don't think about it too much. I don't know that I really feel the need to have every inch of my home covered in security cameras, but I do like the idea that the drone could, for example, go to check out what's going on if one of my smoke alarms' temperature sensors reports that one spot in the house is all of a sudden hotter than it should be.

If you're ready to enter this brave new world of security, you'll have to wait a bit longer: The Ring Drone Camera isn't expected to ship until January 2027, but you can sign up to be alerted when it is available for preorder now.

The all-new M6 MacBook and the touch display PROLED XDR have now arrived, and we are taking a look at some of our favorite accessories to upgrade the experience.

From the latest Apple Magic Keyboard and Trackpad, as well as its World Travel kit, we also have MacBook stands to tidy up your workstation, expandable storage, charging stations for your desktop, and our favorite mouse solutions. The gear collected below might give you some good ideas on how to elevate your new MacBook rig, just be sure to score the 2026 Apple Polishing Cloth at $9 before it sells out again – the only way to clean a MacBook display properly.

I use my MacBook Pro docked at my desk, so an external keyboard and trackpad are must-haves. I’ve used Apple’s Magic Keyboard and Magic Trackpad for as long as I can remember (alongside a Logitech MX Master mouse, as Ben recommends below). I think using Apple’s own peripherals provides a consistent experience whether I’m using my MacBook Pro docked or out on the go.

Apple’s new charging gear now live from $19: World Travel Kit, AC Connector 2, 140W, more

While I’m personally a trackpad guy through and through, I know plenty of people who prefer a mouse, and the power users among them all agree on which one.

#3403. Gang Members Allegedly Target Wrong Car in Drive-By, Kill 12-Year-Old Boy

Three alleged gang members are facing federal charges after prosecutors say they shot at a car they believed belonged to a rival gang member ... but instead ended up killing an innocent 12-year-old boy named Kade Lewin.

24-year-old Ousmane Diallo, 26-year-old Mayel Bussereth and 25-year-old Jonah Luc are charged with racketeering and firearm-related offenses in connection with the deadly 2022 Brooklyn shooting.

Prosecutors claim that on March 31, 2022, the three men who are alleged members of the ICG Barbiez gang drove around looking for a rival gang member.

Per court docs, the three men allegedly drove around the block near East 56th Street and Linden Boulevard several times, apparently searching for their target ... before finally spotting a parked car they believed a rival was sitting inside.

Prosecutors allege they opened fire on the car ... but their intended target wasn't inside. The alleged gang members shot 12-year-old Kade, who was sitting in the vehicle when the bullets came flying. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Another innocent bystander was also caught in the gunfire, but survived.

If convicted, the three gang members could face the death penalty.

#3402. 10 Thriller Audiobooks You Can Finish in a Weekend

Content Warning: This list features a brief mention of assault.Not everyone has the time to sit down and read a thriller every day, which is why audiobooks are the next best thing. Whether you're working in front of a computer, shopping for groceries, or simply traveling from one place to another, listening to a suspenseful story is a great way to keep up with your reading list while getting things done.

The audio format also brings a different dimension to storytelling. Skilled narrators recreate tense atmospheres, build suspense, and put listeners right in the middle of the action. And if you're worried about finding the time to finish one, each title on this list takes no more than 48 hours to complete. From heated courtroom battles to unsolved mysteries, here are thriller audiobooks perfect for a weekend listening session.

Step into the world of espionage with Agent Zero. Running for 11 hours and 14 minutes, the audiobook follows Kent Steele, a 38-year-old European history professor at Columbia University. Living a peaceful life in New York with his two teenage daughters, Kent's routine is abruptly shattered when three terrorists abduct him and take him to Paris.

Convinced that their captive is one of the CIA's deadliest operatives, the kidnappers subject him to brutal interrogations and psychological torture. However, Kent has absolutely no memory of ever being a spy and believes they have mistaken him for someone else. As he struggles to make sense of his situation, he begins uncovering the truth about the mysterious past he cannot remember.

Eight hours and 43 minutes is all you need to listen to the horrifying diary entries in The Silent Patient. Six years after a bloody shootout, the once-acclaimed painter Alicia Berenson is now confined to a psychiatric facility. She has no recollection of her husband's murder, and no therapist has managed to get her to reveal the full story.

Hoping to uncover the truth behind her case, psychotherapist Theo Faber steps in to help her. However, as the two perspectives—Alicia's diary entries and Theo's observations—begin to clash, The Silent Patient becomes a classic case of deciding whom to believe: the supposedly guilty victim or the expert trying to uncover what really happened.

For those who want to spend the weekend solving a murder case, The Fourth Monkey takes just 12 hours and 32 minutes to finish. For five years, Detective Sam Porter has been hunting the elusive Four Monkey Killer (4MK), a serial killer who punishes the families of people he believes have done wrong. However, the killer makes sure each murder is anything but ordinary.

When a man dies under suspicious circumstances in a bus accident, it initially seems like the perfect cover-up. But Detective Porter discovers something unusual: a diary and a white box containing a human ear, both bearing the killer's signature. With the next victim already identified, Porter must race against time to stop 4MK before he strikes again.

Not only is Carrie Stephen King's debut novel and arguably one of his most popular works, but the audiobook also runs for just seven hours and 19 minutes. Even better, the narration comes from none other than Sissy Spacek, the original actress who portrayed the titular character in the first film adaptation of Carrie.

No matter the decade, high school is no joke. Having spent her entire life sheltered from the outside world, Carrie White suddenly finds herself at the mercy of her cruel classmates, who see her as strange and backward. What neither they nor Carrie realize, however, is that she possesses immense supernatural powers capable of setting an entire town ablaze.

Four criminal masterminds. One of them was always going to be yours. Here is who comes for you, why they picked you out of everyone available, and what they want from the encounter.

Your nemesis does not want to beat you. He wants to know you completely, and he is patient enough to wait for it. The frightening part is how good the conversation is.

Your nemesis is not after money, territory or revenge. He is after a demonstration, and you are the person he has chosen to prove his point on.

Your nemesis respects you, which sounds flattering until you work out what it means. He chose you because nobody else was worth his time.

Your nemesis has no personal interest in you whatsoever, and that is precisely what makes him unsurvivable. You are not a rival. You are a stop on the way.

At 10 hours and 31 minutes, None of This Is True follows podcaster Alix Summer as she celebrates her 45th birthday. During the festivities, she crosses paths with Josie Fair, a woman who shares her birthday and was born in the same hospital. Intrigued by Josie's troubled marriage to an older man, Alix invites her onto the podcast to share her story.

However, Josie gets a little too personal once the microphones are on. She reveals disturbing details about her controlling husband, troubled daughters, and deeply buried family secrets. While Alix initially seems like the perfect person to listen to Josie's troubles, she can't shake the growing unease that her new guest might be getting a little too close to her own family affairs.

Few things are more heartbreaking than a missing child. Running for 10 hours and six minutes, The Deep, Deep Snow follows Deputy Shelby Lake, who was abandoned as a baby and rescued by a stranger in the freezing cold. Now an adult, she finds herself investigating the disappearance of ten-year-old Jeremiah Sloan.

With nothing but the boy's abandoned bicycle to go on, Shelby begins to suspect that those closest to him are hiding something. Despite the involvement of local police and the FBI, the investigation gradually loses momentum as the trail grows cold. But when a new clue finally surfaces, she must confront a truth that has remained buried beneath the snow.

If you've never had to step inside a courtroom, consider yourself fortunate. Still, those curious about high-stakes legal battles can get a taste of them through The Lincoln Lawyer. Running for 11 hours and 30 minutes, the audiobook follows criminal defense attorney Mickey Haller, who takes on the case of a wealthy real estate agent accused of brutally assaulting a woman.

Despite his client's claims of innocence, Mickey soon notices several inconsistencies in his account. As the case unfolds, the attorney faces a difficult moral dilemma. Should he capitalize on a lucrative case and protect his wealthy client, or put his principles first and uphold the law?

Retirement is still a few weeks away for FBI agent Claire Anderson in The Fifth Victim. At seven hours and 58 minutes, the audiobook follows Claire as she prepares to leave the bureau for good, only to be assigned to a special task force investigating the notorious Color Killer.

Each of the killer’s targets represents one of four ancient archetypes: The Ruler, The Warrior, The Scholar, and The Priest. With four people already dead and a fifth potentially in danger, Claire joins a team of specialists known as S.W.O.R.D. to track down the perpetrator. However, as the investigation progresses, she begins to suspect that the killer may be much closer to home than she initially imagined.

For readers craving a claustrophobic thriller, The Housemaid offers nine hours and 46 minutes of domestic suspense. Struggling to find work because of her criminal record, Millie Calloway accepts a live-in housekeeping position with the wealthy Winchester family on Long Island. At first, her new employers, Nina and Andrew, seem accommodating enough, making the job appear like a fresh start.

However, the family's pristine image soon begins to crack. Millie discovers Nina's increasingly erratic behavior, while the rest of the household staff offers unsettling warnings about her employers. With her finances dwindling and few options for leaving, Millie finds herself trapped in a house full of unanswered questions, wondering whether the Winchesters are as innocent as they seem.

Fact and fiction collide in Verity. Recently adapted into a star-studded film, the audiobook runs for eight hours and 10 minutes and follows struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh, who accepts an unusual job offer from Jeremy Crawford, the husband of bestselling author Verity Crawford. Her task is to complete the remaining books in his comatose wife's popular series.

While staying at the Crawford family's remote lake house to review Verity's notes, Lowen stumbles upon an unpublished autobiographical manuscript containing disturbing revelations about the couple's marriage. As her attraction to Jeremy grows, she also becomes increasingly suspicious of Verity's condition, questioning whether the woman is truly as helpless as she appears.

Verity is a psychological thriller centering on Lowen Ashleigh, a writer hired to complete novels for Verity Crawford, a bestselling author incapacitated by an accident. As Lowen works at the Crawford residence, she unravels unsettling truths about Verity, intensifying the tension within the household.

#3401. 10 Shows Like 'Minimum Wage' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Spinning off of a popular web series, Netflix's Minimum Wage is currently in the middle of a 28-episode first-season run. If that sounds like a lot of episodes for a show in 2026, keep in mind that they're generally less than 15 minutes each, which is perfect for your overloaded to-watch list—especially when they go down so easily. This cringe workplace mockumentary follows the crew of teenagers running a failing pizza place and making (you guessed it) minimum wage; they're under enormous pressure from their boss (Randall Park) to save the business and their one dumb source of income.

The punchy episodes will leave you plenty of time to explore other streaming shows dealing with the utter ridiculousness of the modern workplace. Here are 10 to get you started.

Workplace comedies usually revolve around white-collar office environments (The Mary Tyler Moore Show, 30 Rock, Parks and Recreation, etc.). Like Minimum Wage, Superstore instead follows the staff of Cloud 9, a generic big-box retailer. The show’s deep bench and diverse cast are largely focused on the jokes, but much of that comedy involves the relatable situation of working a job that demands commitment and a smiley attitude in the face of both entitled customers and obnoxious bosses. It's a different venue and age bracket, but a nutty workplace is a nutty workplace. Stream Superstore on Hulu and Peacock.

We're moving away from the workplace and aging things up a bit, but no worries: the name is a little ironic given that the codependent, co-habitating twenty-somethings of the title are hardly mature. Five friends are cohabiting in the childhood home of Samir (Malik Elassal), and dealing with the uniquely Gen-Z humiliations around dating, work, and even health insurance. Only one member of the group has an actual reasonably good job, while career paths for the others include being a temp, waiter, and a part-time ballet instructor. Stream Adults on Hulu.

This offbeat workplace comedy kicks off with a fabulous premise: Jeong Bok-dong (Kim Byung-chul) was a high-level director in a major corporation until one bad meeting saw him demoted. To president! ...of the company's failing Pegasus Mart offshoot. Bok-dong makes it his mission to get revenge by bankrupting the store, hiring eccentrics to execute eccentric, entirely whackadoo plans and accidentally getting Pegasus noticed by customers, who quickly make it more popular than ever. Think The Producers, but in retail. Stream Pegasus Market on Tubi.

It might sound a little (or a lot) niche, but we’ve seen enough headlines about the working conditions at many video game production houses to understand why a workplace comedy set against such a backdrop would make for a dark and juicy comedy. Charlotte Nicdao and Rob McElhenney are the leads, playing a brilliant workaholic and an unsociable egomaniac, respectively, and the chemistry between them gives the show more than enough spark. There's also a four-episode spin-off called Side Quest. Stream Mythic Quest.

A half-hour comedy-drama with an emphasis on the comedy, Gentefied follows three Mexican-American cousins who have built lives in Los Angeles, only to be faced with a new challenge: the looming gentrification of the neighborhood they helped to build via their family's taco shop. Gentefied has a baked-in sense of place and culture and a lot of heart; the second season is even better than the first. Stream Gentefied on Netflix.

Perhaps there's a bit of counter-programming in this dramedy about a couple of scrappy New York City outsiders, but there's a fundamental goofiness to this show about a couple of nice guys who are great at getting themselves into trouble, and equally good at talking themselves out of it. Bryan Greenberg plays Ben Epstein, a quiet guy with any number of big ideas, while Victor Rasuk plays the outgoing, often shameless Cam Calderon; together they manage a startup clothing business with the benefits of neither money nor experience, amiably hustling their way to success, maybe. Stream How to Make It in America on HBO Max and Netflix.

Debuting at the beginning of the Obama administration before getting a surprise revival just a couple of years ago, Party Down is an acclaimed cult sitcom for the ages—lots of laughs, low ratings, and always worth rediscovering. A group of six (or so) struggling LA actors and writers work as cater waiters for a fancy company, with every episode into a new and wildly absurd situation, even as their aspirations far outstrip their actual lives. Stream Party Down on Prime Video and Netflix.

A legitimate sitcom that just happens to be set in Northern Ireland during the violent Troubles of the 1990s, when clashes between nationalists and unionists frequently resulted in violence. It’s a fascinating contrast, brought to life by a writer and creator (Lisa McGee) who lived it. It’s also laugh-out-loud funny—though it doesn’t make any allowances for audiences unaccustomed to Irish accents, so don’t feel bad if you need subtitles until you get the hang of it. Erin, Orla, Clare, and Michelle are joined by James, the only male student at their Catholic girls' school, dealing with normal growing-up stuff in absurd times. This world is a far cry from that of Minimum Wage, but Lisa McGee's sense of the absurd connects both shows—if the setting is a bit more dramatic, the comedy is just as wonderfully silly. Stream Derry Girls on Netflix.

Not a comedy! But about as good an indication of where we are in the modern global workplace as you're likely to find. Hyuk‑jun is a young guy saddled with debt who signs on for some part-time work at a job agency...at 50x the going rate, no less (should've been a red flag). Each new assignment places him in new and increasingly horrific situations, with increasingly arbitrary-seeming rules. But, hey, in 2026, it's a living. Stream Dead-End Job on Netflix.

It's an office (obviously) and not a pizza joint, but the point here is kinda that white-collar jobs in the 21st century can be at least as soul-killing as working customer service. The Office inherited some of the finer tropes of the workplace comedy (mostly involving tossing together a group of weirdos overly invested in their jobs) while also launching a million mockumentary-style shows, running for nine seasons, and becoming one of the most popular shows of its era. Stream The Office on Peacock.

One of the perks of the streaming era is that, unlike the 20-episode seasons of network TV yore, television shows nowadays are in that sweet spot of 6-10 episodes, meaning that you can easily crush an entire season of great TV in a single weekend.

Apple TV certainly is no exception — the streaming service is home to plenty of quick comedies, high-tension limited series and short-story anthologies that are seemingly made to finish before Monday rolls around yet again.

And these three in particular are exceptionally star-studded affairs, despite their comparatively short episode orders, led by A-listers like Jake Gyllenhaal, Matthew McConaughey, Taron Egerton, and Woody Harrelson. Whether you're after a breezy buddy comedy or a slow-burn psychological thriller, here are three Apple TV shows you can binge-watch in one weekend.

Based on the 2010 autobiographical book "In with the Devil" by James Keene and Hillel Levin, this true-crime drama centers on Jimmy Keene, a high school football hero and decorated policeman's son, whose clean-cut life is upended when he is sentenced to 10 years in a minimum-security prison for dealing narcotics.

That all changes when he's given a high-stakes deal with the FBI: Enter a maximum-security prison and befriend suspected serial killer Larry Hall (Paul Walter Hauser, who won an Emmy and Golden Globe award for his chilling work here) to extract a confession, or serve his full sentence with no possibility for parole.

Across six gripping episodes, the moody psychological thriller thrums with unsettling tension and moral complexity. An ensemble cast that includes Sepideh Moafi, Greg Kinnear and the late, great Ray Liotta doesn't hurt, either.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson have always shared a similar mischievousness, one that, according to a long-standing rumor, might be genetic. Speculation that the two Hollywood stars and real-life besties might actually be biological half-brothers started after Matthew's mother, Kay, revealed during a family vacation that she "knew" Woody's father, Charles Harrelson, if you catch our drift.

The actors gamely expand on that rumor in this Apple TV comedy, which was initially conceived as a standalone eight-episode story but might return for a second season, especially after that season one cliffhanger. In the show, McConaughey and Harrelson play fictionalized versions of themselves, who are forced to deal with that bombshell from Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor) while gathered at Matthew’s Texas ranch.

The show is also noted for being a "True Detective" reunion of sorts, as McConaughey and Harrelson starred together in the first season of the popular HBO crime series.

A second season of this legal thriller anthology is soon to come (with a brand-new cast including Rachel Brosnahan and Matthew Rhys), but before that, you should catch up with its excellent first season, a twisty murder mystery starring a stalwart of the genre, Jake Gyllenhaal.

Adapted from Scott Turow’s 1987 novel of the same name, the eight-episode crime drama revolves around Rusty Sabich (Gyllenhaal), a respected chief deputy prosecutor whose life implodes when he becomes the prime suspect in the brutal murder of his colleague-slash-lover (Renate Reinsve). Rusty is left to fight for his career, his family, and his sanity as he maintains his innocence.

Along with Gyllenhaal and Reinsve, the absolutely stacked cast includes Ruth Negga, Bill Camp, O-T Fagbenle, Chase Infiniti, Nana Mensah, Peter Sarsgaard, Kingston Rumi Southwick and Elizabeth Marvel.

Stream "Presumed Innocent" on Apple TV now

#3397. Report: Apple saved over $5 billion in taxes through Singapore and Ireland in 2026

A new Financial Times report reveals how Apple saved billions in taxes in 2026 by shifting profits through Singapore and Ireland. Here are the details.

A few days ago, Apple published its annual Form 10-K, as required by the SEC, containing detailed information about its financial performance and operations for its 2026 fiscal year.

Included in the form, as the FT noted, is information regarding how Apple reduced its tax bill by billions of dollars through its operations in Singapore and Ireland.

For years, Apple’s tax arrangements in Ireland were the subject of scrutiny, culminating in a 2024 ruling by the EU’s top court that required the company to pay €13 billion in back taxes. Apple completed the payment in 2025.

That came a few years after Apple announced plans to bring most of its $252 billion in overseas cash back to the US, following tax reforms introduced during Donald Trump’s first administration.

Since then, to discourage companies from shifting profits to countries with lower tax rates, more than 130 countries have agreed to introduce a minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for large multinational companies, as part of a 2021 initiative coordinated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

Under the agreement, companies that pay less than 15% in a particular country may face additional taxes to make up the difference. The new rules also resulted in an additional $2.5 billion in taxes for Apple in Singapore in 2026, according to the company’s SEC filing.

Ireland adopted the new rules in 2024, followed by Singapore in 2025.

Back to the FT’s report, it notes that new US accounting rules now require publicly traded companies to disclose when their taxes on overseas profits differ significantly from the 21% US federal corporate tax rate.

These new requirements revealed that Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes through Singapore in 2026, surpassing the $2.6 billion it saved through Ireland.

If Apple had been taxed on all of its global profits in 2026 at the US federal rate, it would have incurred a total bill of $33bn — demonstrating the scale of the $5bn tax reduction it received from booking profits in Ireland and Singapore. The company incurred corporation taxes totalling $27bn this year.

The FT also noted that Apple’s effective tax rate in Singapore fluctuated around 10% between 2023 and 2025, but is expected to approach 15% under the new rules. Singapore’s standard corporate tax rate is 17%.

#3396. There’s a Good Reason the NYC Marathon Winners Wore These Watches

Over 60,000 runners crossed the finish line at the New York City Marathon last week. When you think of the elites fighting for a spot on the podium, you might expect to see only the priciest, most feature-packed GPS watches money can buy—historically, this meant the most premium Garmin Forerunners. Looking at the wrists of this year's New York City Marathon podium finishers, though,  you’ll see that Garmin—the name most recreational runners reach for by default—was far from the only brand on the course.

Here are the watches I’ve been able to confirm among the top NYC Marathon finishers:

Men's winner, Andreas Almgren: Coros Pace 4 (sponsored)

Men's runner-up, Yemaneberhan Crippa: Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro (sponsored)

Women's runner-up, Jessica McClain: Garmin Forerunner 570 (sponsored)

Women's third place, Hellen Obiri: Coros Pace 4 (sponsored)

Nonbinary winner, Ryan Montgomery: Suunto Race 3S (almost certainly sponsored, since this watch was released last month)

An important disclaimer: I haven't spoken with any of these athletes. What follows is my opinion, based on what I know running watches offer the people who wear them.

"Garmin" has long been the default answer to "what running watch should I buy?" It earned that spot with reliable GPS, excellent software, and a huge ecosystem. And on this podium, it's represented by a Forerunner 570—a great watch, but at a price tag most runners would struggle to justify.

Of course, sponsorships muddy the water, since athletes wear what their sponsors put on their wrists. But that's exactly the point: Other brands are investing in elite runners because they believe their products can stand next to Garmin's, and it looks like they’re making the right bet.

It's fair to ask whether Garmin's grip is loosening. The company has increasingly pushed toward the fanciest watches with the most features at higher and higher price points. The Forerunner 570 starts north of $500. Meanwhile, COROS, Amazfit, and others are proving that a perfectly solid, competitive watch doesn't need to cost that much. Is Garmin still the best running watch overall? For ecosystem, polish, and depth of features, it's still a strong contender. But "best" no longer means "the only serious option," and the gap between Garmin and the field is narrower than it has been in years. Sponsored or not, seeing two Coros Pace 4s and an Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro among the top finishers is worth noting.

You don’t need an expensive watch to be elite—just look at the cheap running watches worn by the men who broke the sub-two-hour barrier at the London Marathon this past spring. Training load scores, recovery metrics, maps, music, and smart notifications are nice, but they're extras. If you're shopping for a watch, spend your money on the basics being done right, and don't feel pressured to pay for features you'll never use. Everything besides your time and pace is icing on the cake.

Whichever brand you choose, focus on these basics in your running watch:

The New York City Marathon podium shows a running-watch market that's a bit more competitive and intriguing than the era of "just buy a Garmin" suggests. Garmin is still excellent, but now we’re seeing proof that Coros, Amazfit, and Suunto are all making watches good enough for the fastest humans on the planet. If they can trust those watches on their biggest days, the rest of us can probably trust them with our Saturday long runs.

#3395. Bunnie XO To Jelly Roll: How Much For The Poster Of Me You Trashed?

#3393. Billy Bob Thornton’s Classic Thriller Is Still His Greatest Movie 28 Years Later

With the hit Paramount+ series Landman, Billy Bob Thornton has experienced the esteemed late-career Taylor Sheridan-scripted boost familiar to actors like Sylvester Stallone and Kevin Costner. It’s the rare project that can both give a legendary actor some complex new dimensions while also zeroing in on the things that audiences love about them the most. But if Thornton’s oil landman Tommy Norris deals primarily in the actor’s charm and perceptive insights (as well as his ability to throw out one-liners), it’s not necessarily the most reflective of the roles that truly established him as a brilliant actor. Thornton had been in movies before his breakthrough performance in 1996's Sling Blade, an epic character study he wrote and directed, but that movie showed his range, intensity, and grace in a fully three-dimensional role. And it was soon to be followed by one of his best roles ever.

In Sam Raimi’s 1998 film A Simple Plan, Thornton's role at first appears to be somewhat undeserving of his talents. As in Sling Blade, he plays a somewhat simple-minded character embroiled in a story of violence and crime, with Jacob (Thornton) largely playing second fiddle to the machinations of his morally conflicted brother Hank (Bill Paxton) after they discover a wrecked aircraft in the Midwestern wilderness. In a traditional noir twist, the plane has over $4 million in it, a sum of money that could change the lives of the brothers as well as Jacob’s brother Lou (Brent Briscoe). Lou and Jacob enable each other to a degree that evidently annoys the more straitlaced Hank, whose first thought was to turn the money in. Soon, the millions are effectively a noose around their necks.

A Simple Plan now looks like a major career left turn from Sam Raimi, the director who came to prominence in the public eye with films like Darkman and the original Evil Dead trilogy. His mastery of special effects, horror filmmaking, and Three Stooges-esque comedy made him an unusual pick for a film about betrayal, greed, and brotherhood (although he makes room for all three in the scene of the plane discovery). And his career from the 2000s on has largely been involved in the business of superhero spectacle, whether it’s in the Tobey Maguire-starring Spider-Man trilogy or his dire Oz the Great and Powerful. A Simple Plan represents the filmmaker working in a more subdued and moral register, with characters that feel like real human beings, even to the point of not being entirely sympathetic.

Viewers might expect a character like Jacob to be well-meaning and naive, a little brother who’s made some screwed-up decisions. But Billy Bob Thornton captures the glint in his eye when he’s considering the cash, saying that stealing the money makes him “like Robin Hood.” The movie explores the consequences of finding the money on all three men, with Hank offering to take the cash in until the snow melts and the plane is discovered by authorities. But how long can these guys hold onto a secret like this? They’re not exactly criminal masterminds, and Jacob can’t help but accidentally bring up the plane to passersby. In the tradition of great stories of guilt, like The Tell-Tale Heart or Crime and Punishment, the truth is begging to come out, and it does so in the form of violence.

Billy Bob Thornton could make Jacob messing around with a beer interesting. Working with a screenplay based on the novel by Scott B. Smith (whose later book The Ruins would be tamed down in adaptation), Sam Raimi created a sense of detail and liveliness among the characters that Thornton, Brent Briscoe, and Bill Paxton all honor in different ways. They’re not just simple criminals or thoughtless losers, but real guys that seemed to have crawled out of early ‘90s rural Minnesota, in a way that distinguishes the movie from its clearest cinematic relative: Joel and Ethan Coen’s 1996 classic Midwestern crime masterpiece Fargo. While the brothers would eventually cast Thornton in their divisive noir pastiche The Man Who Wasn’t There, their movies tend to have harsher, less redemptive outlooks than Sam Raimi’s take on the material.

Where Fargo opts for dark comedy and farcical tragedy, A Simple Plan mines deep wells of sadness and sentimentality in its story. Thornton’s eyes suggest either a wild hellion or someone racked with pain, depending on the scene. He holds onto the guilt Hank feels after a man eventually dies, becoming something of a scapegoat for the whole criminal conspiracy. He recognizes that he lacks his brother’s respect, and old wounds rise back up soon. The performance lacks the charisma and likability that has come to define much of Thornton’s filmography, but it makes up for it in complexity and empathy, enough so that it garnered a much-deserved Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor. As he takes a character who could be despicable or pathetic and finds incredible grace notes, it’s hard to deny that it’s some of his greatest work.

#3392. This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

If you've seen an uptick in security updates as of late, you're not alone. AI models have become very good at finding new security vulnerabilities throughout 2026. Researchers and hackers alike are increasingly relying on these models in their individual pursuits: Hackers want to find these flaws to exploit them, while researchers want to block hackers from doing so. Microsoft's latest Patch Tuesday update included more than 1,400 patches; meanwhile, Apple's latest security update fixed two iMessage flaws that let both bad actors and innocent parties alike access texts they shouldn't.

Whether you use a Mac or a PC, you probably browse the web with Chrome, or a Chromium-based browser. As it happens, Google's web browsing platform is the latest to receive an important security update—but it's far from the first important Chrome update of the year.

As reported by The Hacker News, Google released a new update for Chrome on Monday that patches nine security flaws. While all vulnerabilities are important to patch, one in particular is more serious than the rest: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component.

Use-after-free vulnerabilities happen when the system frees up a memory location, but a program tries to access it anyway. It's a glitch in programming, but it offers bad actors an opportunity to break into your system. At worst, it allows arbitrary code execution, or, in other words, gives hackers the ability to run their own code in the app or system.

That's bad enough on the surface, but, unfortunately, Google confirmed that CVE-2026-125350 has an active exploit in the wild. The company is keeping other details close to the vest, but it's dangerous nonetheless. At least someone, somewhere, has used this flaw against a target, which puts all Chrome users (as well as users of Chromium-based browsers) at risk.

What's more, this isn't Chrome's first active exploit of the year—this is its eighth. The company is playing catch-up with hackers looking to target users of its browser, which makes sense, seeing as Chrome is by far the world's most popular browser.

If you're using Chrome on your computer, you'll want to update it as soon as possible. Make sure you're running at least versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 on Mac or PC, or 157.0.8103.50 on Linux. To check, click the three dots in the top-right corner of your Chrome window, then go to More > Help > About Google Chrome.

Other Chromium-based browsers may not have the update yet, but they are affected by this flaw. If you use browsers like Microsoft Edge, Opera, or Brave, keep an eye on your updates to install any of the latest patches.

Earlier this year, I put Google Fi’s $35/month unlimited plan to the test against my Visible service — concluding that it’s a great alternative for anyone who wants a hassle-free setup. In my never-ending quest to find the best cheap cell phone plans, I spent the past 30 days evaluating TextNow’s $35.99/month unlimited plan to see how it holds up and what kind of value it offers over the competition.

I actually signed up for TextNow’s free talk-and-text service a couple of years ago, but it lacked the consistent data connectivity and allotment I needed access to while on the go. Now, the MVNO is stepping up its lineup with an unlimited data plan that runs $8.99 per week, or $35 per month if you want to maximize your savings — directly rivaling Google Fi's entry tier, and for a little more, Visible+ Pro.

If you’re wondering whether it’s worth switching to TextNow’s unlimited plan, I’ll break down the data allowances, extra features, and real-world performance to help you decide if it's worth getting over my experience with Visible and Google Fi.

Unlimited talk & text and 2GB data to/from Canada and Mexico

While swapping eSIMs is often an exercise in futility, the setup process with TextNow was remarkably painless. All it took to get the service running was downloading the TextNow app, logging in, and initiating the eSIM setup. Once I entered my phone's IMEI, it took just a few minutes for the eSIM profile to push directly to my device.

The app also made hardware upgrades effortless: I easily transferred the line from my Motorola Razr Fold over to the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, and it’s now active on my Vivo X500 Pro Max. If your handset doesn’t support eSIM, TextNow can still ship you a physical SIM card. Overall, I’m thrilled I didn’t run into any roadblocks when swapping between daily drivers.

Both Google Fi and Visible also offer the convenience of eSIM activation, with Fi delivering the same frictionless setup as TextNow. Visible, on the other hand, has been hit-or-miss in my experience — with one device swap leaving me stuck with technical support for several hours to get it resolved.

While it’s advertised as an all-you-can-eat offer, TextNow’s plan technically offers unlimited data to chow down on each month — but in reality, it comes with 20 GB of premium high-speed data. I’m a power user and could easily burn through that if I didn’t already have other services to lean on, but it should suffice for most people who primarily stay on Wi-Fi.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

On average, I’ve been getting about 80 Mbps down and about 4 Mbps up. These speeds aren’t a home run compared to the 200 Mbps speeds I got while running on Google Fi with ultra wideband connectivity, so you’ll have to wait a bit longer to download massive files onto your phone. Visible offers faster speeds too in my experience, but Google Fi has always been better.

It's worth mentioning the data caps with each: 20 GB for TextNow, 30 GB for Google Fi, and none technically with Visible. In the fine print details, though, Visible says that "in times of congestion, we may temporarily prioritize Heavy Data User's data behind other traffic for the remainder of the cycle." Meaning, it's unlimited data, but "Heavy Data Users" can see their speeds reduced.

In real-world situations, though, TextNow's data speeds were more than enough to stream Instagram and TikTok reels on the mass transit commute home without any buffering.

One of the biggest adjustments is having to rely on the TextNow app for all your calling and texting needs, which requires granting default app permissions during initial setup. Since I tested the service exclusively on Android devices, losing access to my default phone and messaging apps wasn’t a major issue — especially since Google Messages also routes messages over a data network.

The saving grace of being tied to the TextNow app is that the paid tier eliminates the intrusive ads that plagued the free tier when I tested it a couple of years ago. On top of that, the messaging client supports the modern features I rely on, including smooth handling of GIFs, stickers, videos, and emoji reactions.

At this price point, TextNow leaves out two perks I rely heavily on with my primary Visible line: mobile hotspot and smartwatch connectivity. Visible includes both out of the box, while Google Fi’s $35 plan covers smartwatch data.

Even though TextNow technically doesn’t support hotspot functionality on paper, I was still able to toggle the option on my phone and connect in a pinch. Over my 30 days of testing, the connection was never throttled or shut down — though there’s always a risk the carrier could clamp down on unauthorized tethering down the road.

Still, in such a competitive price bracket, it’s tough to overlook these omissions when rival carriers package them in at no extra charge. Visible+ Pro, for example, lumps in both crucial features at no extra cost.

At the same $35 monthly rate, Google Fi simply delivers a more compelling overall package — not to mention free smartwatch connectivity. Add in Fi's dual-network “Super Network” switching to help eliminate coverage dead zones, and it easily stands out as the superior pick.

Visible+ Pro is also a superb option, despite costing a little more at $39 per month. Although, that extra spread does come with welcome additions I simply don't get with either Google Fi Unlimited Essentials and TextNow Unlimited — such as mobile hotspot functionality, smartwatch data, and a robut set of international features.

While TextNow gets the job done, it functions best as a short-term bridge or secondary option. Paying monthly saves you the most money, but having the flexibility to pay $8.99 week-to-week is a solid perk if you only need temporary connectivity in a pinch.

If nothing else, TextNow’s free talk-and-text option remains well worth setting up as an emergency backup for when your primary carrier suffers an unexpected outage.

#3387. High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

Of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much. Dietary protein helps you build muscle, and if you’re trying to lose weight it helps stop you from losing too much muscle along with the fat. It also helps to make meals feel filling. Great! But.

Once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything. Or, they make products where the good-for-you thing features prominently on the label, whether or not there is very much inside. So a lot of packaged food now boasts protein on the label. Here’s what you should ask yourself about those foods:

Take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

It’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. (I've done the math for various body weights here.) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

So if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

I think this is the most important question about protein-added foods. It’s not hard to get protein in a meal; meats, dairy, tofu, beans, and grains all tend to supply plenty. So what is this protein-added thing you’re considering, and are you eating it instead of a traditional meal?

Here’s an example. If I’m heading straight from the gym to run some errands, and I need something to substitute for a meal—yeah, this isn’t great planning, but sometimes it happens—a protein bar with 20 grams of protein is a step in the right direction. Much better than a candy bar, anyway.

But then there are things like this "protein mix" trail mix: 7 grams of protein with 200 calories. A double serving would be 400 calories and only 14 grams of protein. Hardly a great choice if your goal is just to add to your protein intake for the day.

And then there are the chips that my kid, for a time, couldn't stop eating. He loves Doritos and such; on a whim, we bought him some protein chips (yes, these are a real thing). Are they better for him than the equivalent amount of Doritos? Arguably, sort of yes. But then he started arguing that since they have protein, he should be able to eat them in place of dinner. We nixed that, but admit it: Are you having that same argument with yourself, feeling better about a snack food because it contains extra protein? If so, the marketing is working—you’re feeling good about your supposedly healthy choices, even though you’re just eating a bag of chips.

#3385. Today’s macOS updates fix security gap involving eMudhra certificates

Apple today released macOS updates that address a security gap involving compromised eMudhra certificates, after initially blocking them in Safari, Mail, and other apps in October. Here are the details.

A few weeks ago, Mozilla reported that private keys of eight intermediate certificate authorities operated by eMudhra, an Indian digital certification company, had been compromised.

In essence, these certificates are used to establish trust in digital certificates that verify website identities and enable secure connections.

With access to the compromised private keys, bad actors could potentially create fraudulent certificates that appear legitimate, allowing them to impersonate websites and intercept sensitive user information.

In response to the compromise, Apple began automatically blocking the affected certificates on October 19, followed by additional protections on October 23.

These changes were delivered through automatic certificate configuration updates, meaning users didn’t need to install a macOS update to be protected.

While these measures protected Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple’s networking and security frameworks, they didn’t cover all of macOS, as certain command-line tools, including curl and git, could still accept the compromised certificates.

At the time, Apple published a support article with instructions for administrators to manually address this remaining security gap, while promising a fix in a future macOS update.

Today, Apple updated the document to confirm that the fix is now available.

As Apple explains, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, and macOS 15.8.3, released earlier today, prevent the affected command-line tools from accepting the compromised certificates, eliminating the need for administrators to manually address the issue.

The updates also remove five root CA certificates from /etc/ssl/cert.pem, including three additional eMudhra certificates that weren’t part of Apple’s original manual workaround.

Still, for users who are unable to install the latest macOS updates, Apple continues to provide instructions for manually addressing the issue in its support document, along with the names and SHA-256 fingerprints of the 12 affected certificates and five root CA certificates removed by the updates.

Apple also notes that “some apps and tools include their own list of root CA certificates and don’t use Apple’s block or /etc/ssl/cert.pem,” and advises users to contact the developer of those apps and tools.

To read Apple’s full support document, follow this link.

#3384. Everything You Should Know About Black Friday 2026 Sales: Early Deals, Dates, and Retailers

As is often the case with major sales these days, retailers are increasingly blurring the lines between early deals and the official start of a sale. Black Friday sales appear to be becoming a month-long event, with early deals appearing in the first week of the month. If you haven't been paying attention, major retailers have already put out their plans and even started churning out deals. But you're still in time to make this upcoming Black Friday sale a great one. Here is everything you need to know to prepare you for the big sale.

Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving. This year, Black Friday starts at midnight on Nov. 27. Cyber Monday is the Monday following Black Friday, which starts at midnight on Nov. 30.

The major retailers doing sales are the usual: Amazon, Best Buy, Target, Walmart, Home Depot, and many others. Currently, Walmart has publicized its plans already and has early deals available. Best Buy is offering one of the largest Black Friday and Cyber Week sales, with multiple events and early deals. Target has a three-day event. Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you, and don’t stress over finding the perfect timing. The “best” deal will always depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers that can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot.
